title: What Library Cities Is
definition: Library Cities: cities organized around great public libraries.
description:
Library Cities — Signature Edition: cities organized around great public libraries. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature library hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: reading districts rethought, book transit rebuilt, knowledge commons reimagined for the century ahead. Nothing here is presented as established fact — it is a designed future, fully specified.

This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the stack blocks ambition that defines the Signature line.

title: The Signature Vision: Library Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Library Cities.
description:
The Signature vision of Library Cities does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature library hulls program, charter one: master reading districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale book transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate knowledge commons systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Library Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: The library hulls Grid
definition: The library hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Library Cities.
description:
The urban backbone: power, water, data and logistics woven into one reading districts grid that the library hulls district runs on.

In the Library Cities architecture, the library hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the library hulls fails outright — Library Cities stops being Library Cities at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

Maturity varies: some deployments of this piece exist today in simpler forms, while the full Library Cities-grade version remains a research target. The readiness estimator in this database scores it honestly.

t: 2030 — The first library hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first library hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Library Cities roadmap.
description:
The first library hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its reading districts grid and book transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the reading districts results have to replicate outside the lab, book transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and knowledge commons operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed reading districts demonstrations, book transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting knowledge commons uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

Depends on: reading districts, book transit, knowledge commons.

title: Readiness Estimator: Library Cities
definition: Estimates Library Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Library Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a library hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Library Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Library Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Library Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 54748 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where reading districts monitoring, book transit redundancy, or knowledge commons maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Library Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Library Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Library Cities — cities organized around great public libraries.

Phase 1 — Prove (reading districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (book transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (knowledge commons): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (stack blocks): library hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and cultural core-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
